content.text:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for being with us this morning to follow our results teleconference for the first quarter of 2024. As always, this event is being broadcast live from our headquarters in So Paulo and will be divided into three parts. First, our CEO, Mario Leao, will talk about the main highlights of the period and the strategies by which we will continue to direct our growth in the next trimesters. Then, our CFO, Gustavo Alejo, will do a detailed analysis of the performance. And finally, we will have our Q&A session, during which you will be able to interact directly with us. But before we start, I would like to give you some instructions.
We have three audio options on the screen. All content in Portuguese, all content in English, or in the original audio. For the first two options, we will have simultaneous translation. To choose your option, just click on the button at the bottom of your screen. To ask a question during the Q&A session, just click on the hand icon located at the bottom of your screen.
The questions will be answered in the language they are asked. The presentation we are going to do today is already available for download on our R.I. website. And now, I give the floor to Mario Leao to start the presentation. Hello, good morning, everyone.
It's a pleasure to welcome you to our 1st TRI. It's 10.02 now; we're here live with you. And, as always, I'll start with a summary, which I'll develop with Gustavo in a little while, with the main messages of the trimester and the tone of what we want to tell you about the year. In the first block, on the left, we highlight, with some numbers, the evolution of several of the big results accounts and how we are positioning the bank for 2024 and from now on.
So, it's about 2024, but obviously, it's about the next few years. We have a financial margin, year-on-year, that grows 14%. We will detail in a little while that it grows both from the client's point of view and from the market's point of view. We start to have a positive market margin after a long time, commissions, and acquisitions, also growing at two digits. This is super important because it reinforces what we've been talking about with the market for a few years, the need for us to diversify the portfolio and build, in our first big growth cycle, a Santander with a lot of market dependence and a lot of credit dependence, especially in the low-income sector.
And we, since 2022, have been working to continue making credits, but a more and more diversified credit, and we show this with a lot of emphasis in this TRI, and also make a lot more commissions from a wide base and make acquisitions with an emphasis that we had never given. So we show, in this quarter, with a lot of consistency, this diversification of the portfolio with very potent numbers. We have a PDD that also drops two digits year-on-year; it also drops two digits year-on-year, as we will see in a little while, which shows that our strategy of diversifying the portfolio and of building new safras since 2022, with the credit quality that we have been measuring, testing, and retesting, is working exactly as we would like.
There is an expanded portfolio that grows almost two digits. In several portfolios, which are new in portfolios, where we chose to grow more, we have an annual growth of more than two digits or even more. Obviously, we are working to get more, but with a very clear solidity. ROE is already at, or slightly above, our cost of equity, measured by the market average, in the first 3B. Obviously, we have the return of ROE being touched, and in the first 3B, this is already a step in the right direction.
On the right, I highlight, and then I evolve a little more, some great messages, which are from the 3B, but they are more messages for the year, that I wanted to highlight here for you, which are all very important. First, we are in the middle of a transformation. We launched in January and, throughout the first trimester, we developed what we call a very complete transformation in our store model. I will have the chance to highlight a little more in the future, but, in short, we reformat the way we work with stores, the way we work inside stores, and we actually have a much more connected, much more multi-channel experience, using the store as a great element of differentiation and convenience, we started to have the middle-income customer service done through what we call platforms, regionalized platforms spread throughout Brazil, and with that, a much better ability to cover these middle-income customers, which are millions of customers with a huge potential for profitability at our base.
We do, and now we deliver something that I've been talking about here with the market for several quarters, we relaunch, refound our massive income operation. This was literally two days ago, on a Sunday, and I will try to comment a little more with you about it, which is our Movement Starts Now, which is more than a new offer for massive income, it is a complete repositioning of the Santander brand, the way we position ourselves, the way we communicate, the way we talk to the client, and yes, for massive income, which is the great base of our clients and of the whole market, a much more precise positioning, much more assertive, much more simple.
Moving on to slide 5, I will comment briefly, it couldn't be any different, starting with the client's centrality. We are still extremely focused and obsessed, I would say, with winning and maintaining the client's priority, that is, being the most present bank in the lives of our clients. This is our obsession; it's priority zero.
And to that end, we are working hard on all fronts, channels, segments, products. We show, below, on the left, a very positive evolution in NPS. So, year on year, we have NPS improving in a material way in virtually all channels, in all segments. If we look at product by product, we also have important improvements in accounts, cards, and a number of others. So, it means that we embrace, with strength. I would say that we grasp the client's experience theme with a lot of emphasis and have invested a lot in it.
So, obviously, here, we are never satisfied; we want to keep improving, but we have made a material improvement, year on year, and we are still, throughout this year, super focused on that. We have increasingly better customers with SAFRAs. So, that argument that we, in the old SAFRAs, had the profitability challenges that we know well, and that, for almost two years, I have been exposing here to you, along with Gustavo, with the R&D team, we have increasingly better SAFRAs, the profitability of the most recent SAFRAs, the 23 SAFRAs.
So, here, on a 100 basis, we improve the profitability of this SAFRA by 56%, while the 22 SAFRAs also have an important improvement in profitability, and the older SAFRAs, the 21 SAFRAs, have a profitability that is even falling, due to the digestion of this portfolio, where we grow a lot between 2020 and 2021, and we know that, throughout the last few years, and a little bit still in We have a client-based base that grows year on year; of course, we will seek to grow more rapidly. The client-based clients are, without a doubt, the ones that bring more profitability to the client.
So, every model, every strategy is focused, as I said, on the client's centrality, so that we can be the most active bank in the client's day-to-day, and, with that, have more links. Here I highlight some of the growth levers. I'll start with Select.
We've been talking about Select for several quarters now, in a very consistent way. In fact, we've been talking in a very consistent way about almost all the major themes here, which is a sign that the strategy we defined back in 2022 and perfected in 2023 is the strategy we're following, and I hope to talk for many quarters with you about the same major themes for many years. High income is a big focus here at Santander.
We have in Select a powerful lever for growth, for rentalization, for linking, for cross-sell. We had, not long ago, 600,000 clients in Select, and here we are very proud to show the number of 1,400,000. You'll remember that, a short time ago, I talked about the ambition to reach 1 million.
We've reached it; at the end of last year, we had already exceeded 1 million, and we're growing even more for this first quarter. Obviously, we're on an aggressive count to reach 2 million clients in Select. We hope to achieve this in the short and medium terms, but we're growing consistently. We grow by bringing in investors. But we're also bringing in buyers, which is important. Select is not just about investors.
We have almost a third of the APF's credit portfolio in Select clients, obviously with a lower credit cost and a portfolio that is not less than 68 billion of credit in Select. We, along with that, have the best liquid capitalization in history in Select. We'll look at the next page, in retail as a whole, I'd say in the bank as a whole.
So, on the investment side, on the client-investor side of Select, we're doing a better and better job consolidating the strategy we made when redesigning Select almost two years ago, when creating our advisory channel, which we call D2A, and when doing all of this super-integrated with a complete offer for high-end clients. On the next page, which is page 7, I emphasize a little more on the topic of investments. As I said in the beginning, and I have been talking to you since 2022, we had a great gap in the bank's business portfolio.
We recognized this and started to invest consistently in focusing the organization on the topic of passives, on the side of each balance sheet, and being able to consistently redesign the mix of bank captures in Brazil, which has always been more proportionally based on attacks and institutional clients than in retail, be it PJs, retail, be it PFs, mainly, of which 5 billion were from this advisory channel, which is our AAA. We are consolidating the AAA. We haven't even reached 2,000 advisors, which is our public ambition.
But more than a temporary ambition, we think this is the right number to be able to cover, at the level of coverage, of load, of clients per advisor, the lowest load in the entire market, which means a unique ability to give advice to the investor client, which we believe we have here in Santander. We have, in this AAA channel, an average of 3.7 million per advisor in the quarter, which is a very powerful number, already a leap compared to last year, which means that we are consolidating this strategy.
Without a doubt, we want to grow even more, but we are already at a level that makes us very happy. Toro is our digital broker, which we are increasingly seeing ways to integrate and be able to have a unique approach to the part of physical person brokerage, multi-channel, but based a lot on digital.
Toro is also growing solidly in the TRI; it has a growth of more than 3 billion, it is reaching almost 20 billion in assets under custody, and it also has, as well as in the PFI retail, as a whole, a super high NPS. Our private has a growth of almost 2 billion in the TRI; we hope to accelerate this throughout the year. Once again, it is recognized as the best international private bank in Brazil and is consistently gaining shares.
So, as a whole, the message of investments is the organization's key has also turned to passives. We are looking at both On and Off Balance in a much more solid, much more focused way. I am sure that this will be one of the great levers of differentiation in the richness of our results and of the business portfolio over the next years. Here I cover, in two pages, what we have called, since 2022, strategic business. This is to emphasize to the market where we chose to focus and why we chose to focus, and how we are delivering. So, I will highlight four big businesses.
The first is the business of cards, which has been gaining more prominence here in the publications, while since the middle of last year, we have been selling cards in a more emphatic way. We are back to the growth of cards, literally with the same level of appetite, but with much more advanced technology in terms of the ability to personalize customers, ability to differentiate the non-customer that we want to bring here, the non-customer that we don't want, and a much better ability to activate the customers that we already have in the bar, which I will talk more about in a little while.
So, in practice, we are growing cards, selling cards in a broader way than we did a year ago. This is bringing an increase in turnover, year on year, which is this first graph on the left. And in each quarter, we are increasing our total turnover.
We are actually increasing the average spending per customer and also increasing the customer base for the first time in a long time. I would say that for the first time since 2021, we have had an increase in the customer base in the quarter, year on year, which is these 3% that I show here in the second graph, and a turnover that grows even more. That is, we grow the customer base, the customer base grows again, and we have an average spending per customer growing a lot. On the right side, I talk about the consigned business. I've been talking about it every quarter with you.
We have consistently, since 2022, worked a lot to earn the quota and earn it with quality, with both the right price and the right level of risk. We have better credit performance than the average of the system. And even so, we are earning quotas. And even so, we have a record level of production. The portfolio grows to 72 billion euros.
And we have the highest level of production that we've ever had, which the graph here shows as well. So, in summary, Consignado is an extremely competitive product, as we know, which has practically all the incumbents, medium banks, and also digital ones coming in. We are very confident in the strategy, in our multichannelity in Consignado, in our diversification. We have a very strong and growing Consignado in the NSS, we have a very consolidated Consignado in governments, and we have a very strong Consignado on the private side.
Here, zooming in on the financial side, we have a business that is a market leader, as we know, that continues to work with a rate above 20%; we are at 21%, approximately. Here, it is not the rate by which we are doing well; we are also at record levels of production in the financial sector. We started the year with the same effort that we finished last year.
In fact, since August last year, we have been working very hard on the recovery of the financial sector. Why did we reaccelerate in the financial sector? Because we saw, during 18 months, that all the adjustments that we had to make in the portfolio, we made, and we saw that it was time to resume, always with higher ratings, so we continue with a very high rigor, and I would say with a great restriction of the customer base with which we are operating more, we are managing to penetrate, and the portfolio is growing, with very positive production, given both our relationships with the stores, as well as with Agro has a year, not agro as a whole; some of the cultures have a more challenging year this year, on the soy and corn side, while some others are having a super positive year.
Santander embraced agro 8 or 9 years ago. This embrace will continue this week, including the Agro Show Week. We will be there, with presents and photos.
We continue to grow in agro. Possibly, we will have a less strong level of growth than we have had in the last two years, when we practically doubled the portfolio, but here you can see that we have grown a few more B's in the portfolio. And we continue, of course, monitoring each case super closely, but with a medium and long-term approach, as it has to be in the case of agro.
Here we are quickly covering business, or businesses. We, on the left side, covering SMEs, still have the ambition to double this business. We believe that we can double this business in a few years, and we will look for that.
Of course, growing together with the clients. We continue to grow in credit, and we continue to grow in transactionality. Here, giving a little more of a zoom on what we are doing with the service to small businesses, we take, in practice, the service of small businesses within the stores. In this new redesign of the stores, we put the specialists of small businesses spread out around the stores, covering what we call the micro-regions.
We expand this team a lot, we put in many more hundreds of people and a whole management structure to be able to have the service of small businesses, in fact, much more pulverized. We brutally reduce the average coverage radius.
We often increase the number of visits per day that each specialist can do. So, basically, what we want, in short, is to dominate the micro-region, dominate the surroundings of the stores, having the stores as a hubs, but no longer having the figure of the specialist there in the store, serving the flow that comes and continues to come into the stores. So, we start to have a much more in-house service for the client, much more where the PJ is, than doing what the PJ has to come to the bank for.
This is quite powerful, quite innovative. We believe that we will have consistent gain from here. On the side of big companies, we still have very solid growth for the franchise. We are still a leader in several markets where we have been operating for years. We are number one or number two in several league tables here consistently.
We have a franchise of investment banks that is consolidating more and more. It is true that the first quarter was not the most promising in the world for investment banks, in M&A, and especially in the variable income market, but in fixed income, where we have a very consolidated franchise. We also had a very good first quarter as a market, so we have a very positive dynamic in the fixed income market, while the variable income and M&A are still to be desired, but we hope that throughout the year, they will improve. But the franchise, as a whole, grows, it grows in revenues, and it grows in profitability. We have been very disciplined here at PJ Grande in not necessarily looking for quotas, obviously with a great focus on profitability.
And with the fixed income capital market quite strong, we have competition from funds and market operations, and we often just let the operations pass and act more as a distributor than as a loader, as a balance. Here, on my last page, and then I'll pause, here, perhaps, is the most important theme of today's session because it is the summary, and I'll make it brief, of our refoundation, of our repositioning, and the relaunch of our Massive Income Strategy.
Before I talk about the proposal and the repositioning itself... We call it Começa Agora. Why are we doing this now? What is the context for which we have decided to do this now?
First of all, we're a digital-first operation. We're not digital-only, and that's good because we're a multi-channel operation. But we're digital-first. More than 90% of our clients use an app. We have a reduction of more than a third in the number of visits to stores.
We have seen a reduction of more than 20% in the number of calls to our center, to our remote service. So, the client was educating themselves, we were educating the client, and, of course, the market was also educating the client to make our relationship mainly a digital one. Second, we have a very powerful remote conversational agent. We have First Call Resolution, that is, the ability to answer customers on the first call, which is reaching 97%.
We have seen an increasing increase in the use of chat within the remote channel. So, the remote channel that we built it, and most of the payment banks built it, by phone, and we are increasingly migrating from phone to chat. And this chat, which is both the bot chat, the chat with non-generative artificial intelligence, and then the human chat, we are bringing the DNAI element, the Generative Artificial Intelligence, to support us, to bring productivity gains, to bring the ability to serve the customer.
So, the digital context, on the one hand, and the remote conversational context, on the other, made us launch this redesign of the stores at the beginning of the year. I have already commented on the theme of small businesses, quickly commenting on the average income. What we do, as I said at the beginning, is that we also take the specialist, him or her, who served the average-income customers, and creates the concept of platforms, Van Gogh platforms, medium-income platforms, which are, basically, physical spaces that are inside the stores, in sections, or in other offices that we have spread throughout Brazil. We have almost 200 offices like this.
So, we are serving, in a regionalized way, our medium-income customers, and with that, allowing these specialists, him, or her, to provide proactive service and also reactive, in a much more assertive way. So, here we hope to take a huge leap in our ability to bring medium-income customers to Santander. It is just beginning; I will update the market over time, but this is an important launch that we also did at the beginning of the year. Thus, the store is no longer the owner of a client portfolio.
This is a leap that we take. The store had its own result, coming from the result of the real estate loan made two years ago, from the credit card sold a year ago, and so on. If we take that away, the store becomes a point of sale and a point of service.

And then there's a fourth quarter flat, and now, in fact, it starts to grow with a little more strength. How would I answer your question? Block A, the liquid margin of acquisitions. This one tends to fall, in fact, because of Selic. So, Selic will fall a little slower, so the detractor element of this line dilutes the time a little more.
But we already know this, as you all know, so we are working to compensate for this in acquisitions with volume and mix. Mix is passive, with having more of that float resource that is in the account. We have, as all banks have, the instruments of profitability to be able to have a good margin there. Obviously, we don't just want to count on floating money, so we have to bring the investor client here, then all the investment agenda, select and beyond. So, we are going to compensate for Selic's fall with volume and mix. So, we expect to have a positive performance here, even though Selic's strength is throwing this line out there.
Knowing this challenge that we have in the margin of acquisitions, we will continue to do well, and with even more strength, of course, the active part, the credit, and extended portfolio part. And here, we are actually going to look for the same type of mix that we are building here. So, you should expect an average spread level similar to the one we had back there, where the clean portfolio, the low-income portfolio, the ratings, on our scale of 1 to 10, rating 5, 6, 7, were much more present than they are today.
No, because we don't have the same mix, we don't want to have the same mix, we are working with a little on rating 8 clients and a lot on rating 9 and 10 clients. Each bank has its own scale, but you can see a dimension of where we are cutting. So, we want to have a clean exposure with 9 and 10, and even collateralized, as in the financial sector, as in the consignado, we also want to have higher ratings. So, our average rating goes up a few points, certainly, from 21 to 22.
So, we shouldn't expect, in the first line, the same level of gross spread, but obviously, we should expect the level of liquid PDD spread to improve over time because I think that's what we are showing. So, this doesn't necessarily happen in the same tree, where first you build the portfolio, you digest the portfolio, we make fewer agreements, we launch the results more, the cases that we see that we won't be able to recover in time, and Gustavo covered this a little bit, he can cover more.
So, temporarily, it's not all exactly in the same tree, but the direction of a first line of liquid credit costs, becoming more and more healthy, and obviously the digestion of the past portfolio, also flowing, this gradually creates a jawbone in this line of credit, let's call it that, that we believe we have already shown in this tree and will continue to show. So, we are positive, in summary, about how this line will behave during the year. In that case, if you go down on one side, we compensate for volume and price, and on the asset side, we will continue to grow, but with the same type of mix of products and with the same type of customer portfolio that we have sought. Gustavo, I don't know if you want to add anything. Yuri, that's exactly what it is.
So, there is no comparison between the previous portfolio and the current portfolio. In the current portfolio, we will continue with the same dynamics, so we will continue with the same ratings, we will continue with the same composition of products per client cluster, so we will continue with the same profile per microportfolio, as I said. We are advancing a lot in CP with some kind of guarantee; we had higher volumetricity with CP Clean, so we effectively change the entire composition of our portfolio. If the CDI falls, we make a composition in the passive, but also make a composition in the asset to balance it.
What we are looking for is that the liquid spread is getting bigger and bigger, and this opens up over time. This is a little of the dynamics we have. Perfect, thank you Gustavo, thank you Mario. Good luck with the results and congratulations again.
Thank you. Now we are with Eduardo Nishio from Genial. Hello Nishio, good morning. Hello Camila, good morning, everyone.
Good morning Mario, and Gustavo. Congratulations on your results. I would like to talk a little more about retail, specifically your strategy, Massificado. Congratulations on the launch. Retail has changed a lot in this cycle, and you came up with a new strategy. I would like you to talk a little more about the profitability you expect, what happened in this cycle, talk a little more about the target audience, if it is the open sea, if it is low income, your vision for Massificado and retail. Thank you. Great, Eduardo. Thank you, Unknown.
It's a good hook for us to talk a little more about massivism, so I'll try to be brief here. These are the key themes. We recognize that the client has evolved. He has evolved in the type of demand, in the type of relationship he wants to have, in the type of principality he is willing to give.
Today, the client has at least five active accounts on average and has almost four active accounts for each client. So, the way the client defines principality has changed a lot over the years, and, therefore, the ability of each digital bank, or bank, it doesn't matter; we are all digital, to work to earn, if not all the client's principality, a good part of it, also has to change a lot. So, this is super clear; we recognize the market as well.
We also recognize that the way we, and possibly the whole market, approach credit for this massive audience had to evolve. Between 2020 and 2021, the market as a whole granted credit, possibly beyond what these clients were able to absorb. Hence, the credit costs for the following years are much higher in all the banks in the market, which means that we tested, in a hard way, and learned in a hard way, the elasticity of low-income income, Eduardo.
So, what we bring from learning as a starting point for this new offer is a much finer and more precise notion of how elastic the income capacity of this audience is, which, obviously, is much less elastic than the average and high-income, and PJ itself. So, with a much better and much finer understanding of how much fits in the pocket of this low-income, and, therefore, what size of exposure we can have with each client, and what exposure is worth having with that client, which depends a lot on whether I have the transactionality of this client or not, because it's no use being the element that brings even small credit to that client, it will use my credit to pay another bank, and then I end up with an adverse selection.
So, in the end, I would say that our maturity as a management here is to better understand the context, to better understand the little elasticity that the low-income has, and to better understand the need of this client to be here at home, transacting with us, and choosing us as the principal, or in the direction of choosing us as the principal, so that we can, in fact, have a better chance in the use of that limited income to pay the So, that's the context.
It's the context that, certainly, the whole market recognizes today, so there's no great confidential information here. How do we approach this in a different way? We approach it with a starting point that is a much, much simpler offer than any offer we've ever had. An offer that is absolutely free, as we talk about in the video that you saw, free without asterisks. This is super important; it's not that we had asterisks before, but all offers, historically, incumbents and digital ones, correctly provoked, and, in a way, even criticized incumbents for this, So, we here wanted to make an offer, in fact, without conditions.
So, we act with an account and a card which is free for life, which is, in fact, free forever. And, well, where are we going to get the profitability from this? Of course, taking the client from an offer that, in addition to being free for life, brings unlimited withdrawals, which is something for those who withdraw money. This public still has the use of money for a while, and it is still relevant, so we believe that a limited withdrawal is a nice proposal.
And we also bring the element of 10 days without interest, which Santander has super strong, linked to a strong PIX key. So, the client who puts the strong PIX key here, on the cell phone or CPF, we will give them 10 days without interest, which, obviously, is a huge differentiation element.
So, adding these elements, or equalization, or differentiation, we will deliver a super simple and digital experience, with a well-integrated human conversational, and with the stores as a convenient element, as I said earlier. So, we believe that the new offer of Começa Agora, Começa Agora is the positioning as a whole, and the new offer of Free, Eduardo, will bring, deep down, a chat app in relation to what we didn't have and a positive differential in relation to what we already had, and we package it in a super simple and direct way for the client.
So, we believe that, from now on, we will bring back this client who was here but was inactive. To give you an idea, we have more or less 30 million inactive clients, our total base is 60 and a few million, and our asset base is just over 30. So, in practice, half of our clients are inactive, so there is a lot of what we are looking for here, which is to activate the inactive clients, to answer this part of your question.
And there is something, of course, about open sea capture, but it is not the open sea that we did in 2021, and possibly a good part of the market; it is the open sea, first, proportionally much smaller, much more qualified, with much more information, much more intelligence in the use of data, to understand who this differentiated client is. So, today we are much safer to look at even this open sea client, which weighs less than in the past.
But a good part here will be clients who are already in the database and who are inactive, or who are in the active database but are not so happy with the offer and are gradually leaving and giving priority to others. We want to recover these clients, reactivate the inactive ones, and, yes, make client acquisitions, but with a super-big differentiation between what we want and what we don't want. Perfect, thank you very much.
Thank you. The next question comes from Brian Flores from Citibank. Hello, Brian.
Hello Camila, and thank you very much for the opportunity to ask questions. Taking advantage of Yuri and Mario's question, which was about credit costs, how should we think about them as a percentage of the portfolio? And also, how does that connect with the renegotiation strategy, which seems to be running at lower levels now? Thank you very much.
I will start with the second part. We have already commented that we have changed the renegotiation strategy. The renegotiation dynamic remains much more selective, and the renegotiation portfolio, over time, will be reduced precisely because of the fact that we have the old portfolios being digested, as Mario mentioned.
Credit costs, at the rate that we are growing, and with the credit discipline that we have, and no change in the risk profile, it has a positive tendency to reduce credit costs. It will depend a little on how we grow and where we grow, but we have already seen a very important evolution in the last 12 months, and we may have future evolutions, but it also depends on how much we advance in the portfolios, given that we have a lot of confidence in the credit performance, and all the new portfolios that we are producing are performing exactly as we expect, so there is no surprise in relation to the new portfolios, also in relation Perfeito, obrigado.
We will now switch to English with Tito Labarta from Goldman Sachs. Good morning, Tito. Hi. Good morning, Camila.
Good morning, everyone. Thank you for the call and taking my question. Actually, a bit of a follow-up to Brian's question on the cost of risk, but more on the asset quality side. We saw, you know, the MPLs were still sort of flattish in the quarter.
I know there's maybe some seasonality in 1Q, but the SME MPLs did go up a little bit. So just how are you thinking about asset quality from here? I mean, it seems that we're past the worst of it, particularly if your provisioning levels are coming down. But at any risk to that, how do you think asset quality can evolve from here? Let me just, hi, thank you, thank you for participating. So I'm just starting off, and now I'll hand it over to Gustavo.
So the broad message, taking the opportunity for a question is, we're very comfortable with the portfolio we're building, the portfolio we've been building for the last two years, I'll say, and obviously, with the benefit of having now two-year-old vintages, one-year-old vintages, six-month-old vintages. With all that we can back test. And we continuously do that every time more and more, more precisely, and we take the small adjustment decisions much faster than we did before. So all that points to the direction that we're managing with better tools with much more modern policies and models, and the vintages are behaving well, on average. So, yes, there's seasonality, there's...
The elements that you see in the presentation relate much more to the digestion of the older vintages, which we've been embracing differently for a year already in terms of the acuerdos, the renegotiations than we did before. So Gustavo can comment better, but the direction I wanted to share with you is that, yes, we're very comfortable with the way the portfolio is behaving, the direction we're taking, and how the new vintages since 2022, by the way, are behaving. So with that, Gustavo, please. Exactly that. There are no changes.
I mentioned last quarter that potentially we'll see some volatility in the overs, but it's totally related to the old vintages and the old portfolio. So it's everything under control. So, uh, uh, in terms of the future and credit quality, is everything really under control? Okay, great.
Thanks, Mario and Gustavo. Thank you. Let's go back to Portuguese now, with Gustavo Schroden from Bradesco BBI.
Good morning, Schroden. Good morning, Cami. Thank you. Good morning, Mario, and Gustavo.
Congratulations on the results, really strong. I'd like to talk a little bit because I think we're missing a part of the equation. People have discussed the NII a lot; we talked about segmentation, product, and mix, but I'd like to talk a little bit about portfolio growth. I think it's an important component for the NII. The portfolio grew 5% year on year. I'd like to understand if there is room to accelerate this?
I think we should see this portfolio growth accelerate over the next three quarters. Do you think we can get close to 8% to 10%? Do you think it's a reasonable number for us to have here in terms of portfolio growth? And also, talk a little bit about the mix, right?
Not in the segmentation, but anyway, we saw strong growth focused on designating the vehicle. The trend is the same. And if I can get a hook here, I think portfolio growth can leverage another point, which is profitability. I'm a big fan of Roy, from 10, 11 to 14.
Do you think we can get to the end of the year with Roy closer to his recent past? Before all this deterioration that happened in the asset quality system, which made everyone hold their portfolio growth, the influence rate went up, and the impact would go up. I'd like to know if we can go back to dreaming of that Roy, closer to 18, 20.
Obviously, I understand the limitations; it's not guidance I want, but I just want to know if that's the way. Thank you. I'll start with the portfolio topic, and then I'll come to profitability. As I said, and Gustavo reinforced it later, we are growing exactly in the portfolios we want to grow. We don't have a goal here of growing the same, 10%, 100%, 8%, 12%, the same for everyone. It wouldn't be a smart way to manage the bank, and it's not what you expect from us either.
We choose the businesses in which we want to consolidate leadership or gain share, but we never want to gain share without profitability and at the cost of the credit cost of 6, 12, 18 months. You don't see us growing that way. So, we choose some businesses and detail more here in the promotional disclosure. We decided to grow here.
Cards are growing. We spoke little during a year and a half of cards because we were in a deceleration module, and we, since the third trimester, have commented more, still a little shyly. Now we're going to start talking a little more because we're starting to have the consolidation of our strategy of growing again in cards. So, I would say that when we think about the size of the growth, of course, we're not going to go all out, as you know, but we expect to grow as much as the average market is expected by Febraban. We expect, in fact, to be able to...
Given that in some businesses we know we will be able to grow more and will..., which are businesses, obviously, with a higher level of profitability, if we do it well, and I really believe that we are doing it well, we have everything to have growth here that should be equal to or greater than the market growth. In large companies, I will not tell you the same thing, because, as I said, then Gustavo reinforced, we will look for, as in everything, actually, a huge discipline of profitability.
So, where I managed to have marginal ROIs in that positive operation, and that generated economic profit above our ROIs, we, on average, if the credit risk is good, we will do it. We will look at the operation, and we will look at the cross-sell capacity on top of that operation. The attack operation, of course, has a lot of cross-sell in services, mandates, and such.
So, we will always look at the customer's vision in a way, but there will be cases where even in the customer's vision it will not make sense to do it, and we will become, as I said, a distributor and not so much a credit loader. So, here we are not in a sprint of, ah, I have to grow 8, 10, or 5, up to here in the year. We have a slight drop, but it absolutely does not worry us, because the business itself is making more money than it did in the last quarter and last year.
So, we have pretty good profitability in our attack operation on large companies. Here, it may be that we grow less than the market, but it is already ex-ante. I'm not saying it will be, but if it happens, it will be because of super-fine capital discipline, and we will compensate for this with growth, also with capital discipline, in the other operations, as we showed in the first three. So translating all this into profitability.
Well, since I will be disciplined in the attack and only do the operations that are ROE-acquitted, and since my retail operations, PF, PJ, and finance, are operations with very high profitability, of course, as long as we know how to select the right clients, and the right products, we hope that the recovery that you mentioned of ROE, which was a good recovery, will continue gradually over time. What are we looking for without guidance?
We are looking to consolidate a mid-teens, then consolidate a mid-to-high-teens, and then we will work hard to come back at some point to a very high-teens or 20s. Obviously, we are not at this level in the short term, but we are redesigning the operation, executing a very disciplined strategy, to be able to meet this. What I would like to finish is that the quality of the portfolio that is delivering this ROE, and that will deliver the ROE of the next tree, is a very different quality, much more diversified and, therefore, sustainable.
So we are less focused on the speed with which I go up the ROE 1, 2, 3 points, and yes, with the solidity that I deliver this higher ROE, to be able, from there, to seek the next leap, and so on.
Perfect, super clear, thank you and congratulations once again. Obrigado, Gustavo. I would like to thank you all for being with us this morning. After this videoconference, I and the entire team of relations with Santander investors are available to clarify any remaining questions. Thank you very much, have a great day and see you next time.

Camila Toledo
[Interpreted] Good morning, everyone. Welcome. We are here in our headquarters in São Paulo live for our third quarter 2023 earnings conference call. Today, this event will be divided into 3 parts.
First, our CEO, Mario Leao, will talk about our strategy and the main highlights of the quarter. Then Gustavo Alejo, our CFO, will provide a detailed analysis of all the members that were highlighted during the period. And lastly, we will host a Q&A session during which you will be able to interact directly with us.
I would like to remind you that we have simultaneous translation, so you can choose whether you want to follow the presentation in Portuguese, in English or just simply using the original audio. I would also like to tell you that the presentation that you are about to see is already available in our IR website.
Now I will turn the floor to Mario Leao to begin the presentation.
Mario Roberto Leao
[Interpreted] Hello. Good morning, everyone. It's a great pleasure to be with you again. This is a different format, and I hope you enjoy. We are constantly evolving. We are here live. It's now 10:02. I'm glad to have the opportunity to tell you more about our performance together with our IR team and Gustavo.
I would like to start on Page 4 -- Slide 4. Here, I highlight the most relevant aspects of the quarter and then we will elaborate further on the following slides. And I'll talk about the quarter and the outlook for the year. The most important highlights are right here on my left.
First of all, for quite some time, we've been telling you, I mean, during previous conferences, Camila and I participated in a relevant conference in New York, and we've been talking to several investors throughout the past 9 months, and we talked about the diversification of our portfolio.
This is quite an important aspect because we build our major growth cycle with a great emphasis on loans and specialty loans to low-income people in different markets. And certainly, we look at the past, and we realized that we had to have a more balanced portfolio with a pluri-annual investment.
It's a permanent investment because it takes a few years in funding and also fees that we had a relevant business, but we thought it had to be even more relevant. This year, we clearly know that the strategy is being executed. We've seen some progress. And certainly, we will continue to pursue looking at these two areas of diversification.
The second highlight is that we continue to see a very positive evolution in terms of quality of assets. I can say that in all of our metrics, NPL formation, coverage ratio, cost of credit and even the [ ALL ] results evolved, and this makes us very pleased because it shows consistency in everything we do. We've been talking to the market in a very patient and consistent way in the past 3 quarters. And now we are just consolidated everything we said in the past quarters.
Now we see that we are capable of resuming growth in a very conscious and focused way with a more constructive buys from now on. And we will show you some figures in a moment.
In terms of our financial margin, we see -- in terms of our NII, we see that we involved and Gustavo will talk more about it in terms of clients. Things are being consistent, even though the evolution was small, but this is important because in the past year or 9 months, we were able to build our portfolio with more selective clients and clients that have a better cost of credit.
And to continue, we have a very good agenda of productivity and efficiency. And I constantly highlight that because that's part of Santander's culture. And this is important because it means that we can continue to invest in growth and this will not compromise the result of the bank as a whole.
Speaking about our net income, net income is important in the quarter because certainly, we want that progress to continue, and we will see that with time. But we posted 18% growth in ROE that had a significant improved BRL 2.7 billion vis-a-vis the previous quarter and ROE is going from 11% to 13%.
In terms of our priorities for the year, to my left and to your right, I see here 3 highlights. And these are very consistent with everything we've been talking about, enormous focus on customers. Well, everybody talks about their clients, but Santander has a very high obsession with clients. We are not running after increasing the volume of clients. Of course, this is important, but we are less concerned with our ranking of clients, but much more on how do I monetize? How do I become the principal bank for the customers. And this is our strategy and everything we are doing in terms of technology, innovation, focus on priority businesses with a view on the customer has to do with that. And I'll give you some insights about that as well.
On Slide 5, I bring more details about customer centrality First of all, I would like to highlight our major obsession in our pursuit for principality. This quarter, I have some very good numbers to show you. This is quarterly growth of 3% of loyal customers. At Santander, we have a very high bar in terms of what we call a loyal customer. But this is a metric that is very consistent. We are growing 3% quarter-on-quarter. And so this is a figure that makes us very pleased because this number increases due to several drivers that -- on which we've been working consistently.
One is a great focus on CRM. We are totally redesigning our CRM strategy. We are trying to provide better and more customized offerings instead of having one size fits all offering, we are now customizing communication. We are connecting customers along his or her journey, and this has driven us to a total review. I mean we are actively reviewing our value proposition in all segments.
In the next coming slides, I will talk more about Select, our high-income proposition. This is growing at a very good pace. We have a good offering of products and services that we need. We almost need to develop any new services or products. Our agenda has been more focused on simplifying the offering rather than creating additional offerings. And with that, we gain agility. We gain in our capacity to serve customers and as a result, we gain more loyalty.
The NPS on the top of the screen, we've been consistently talking about NPS every single quarter. In this quarter, we certainly have many good news in all channels, in all segments, we've seen an evolution. I would like to highlight our remote channel with a year-on-year evolution of 32% of NPS. And in our corporate line, this is the first time we talk about corporate NPS, it's 39%, but I know we have a lot of room to improve, but this number had remained at 20% to 25% for quite some time. So we increased by 19 points, and we are certainly committed to pursue higher levels of NPS.
And to conclude on this slide, we have some elements that show the consolidation of our revenue that I showed down below, and we will cover them in more details further on. We grew almost 7% quarter-on-quarter in terms of fees. It shows that volume is growing, transactionality is growing. And with all of that, we are bringing customers to renegotiate and to increase the transactions with us.
Now I talked about high-income customers. It's been a year since we redesigned our value proposition for high-income customers. And I've been constantly telling you about that because we are progressing the way we expected. The business is performing well and NPS, as a result, is increasing as well. The customer base is increasing almost 50% year-on-year. We go from 674,000 to almost 1 million.
About a year ago, I established a public commitment that we would hit the mark of 1 million Select customers until the end of the year. And I'm sure that we will get there. Our revenue in terms of Select credit is growing consistently. So everything is according to plan. We are looking at everything with great focus, but we believe that we have a big differential in terms of investment model, the AAA that I will talk about it soon.
Our store model, we have great stores scattered throughout the country and our service 24/7. And now to complete the offering, this is a spoiler, but I'm already talking about it. So in a few weeks, we will launch Select Global and offer for international transactions. It will be launched in the next few weeks. And in a month's time, we will have a major launch to the market. And then finally, there will be nothing else left to do. I mean, so Select customers can have an international account and have access to that account through our app. And certainly, with that, customers will be even more loyal and will be closer to us.
Next slide, we show you our investments. Here, I highlighted a few elements to tell you about our strategic focus that is now bearing fruits and becoming more material. And certainly, this will bring about better results. So strategically, we decided that we had to change the funding mix of the bank. We never had any liquidity issues, but we had and we still have a lot of our funding coming from wholesale. Wholesale will be large corporate or institutional customers. There is nothing wrong with that in terms of volume, but in terms of pricing, yes.
So we are strategically and structurally changing our funding mix from mostly on wholesale to mostly on retail, especially in individuals and corporates as well. We have some data. Of course, we want more and we will go after more. But we already see some relevant figures. If we go back to 2021, the numbers is to your left, that was negative in the year-to-date in 2021. So now we will increase the numbers further and we are working hard to improve even further.
In terms of retail, emphasis on AAA, our strategy or our response to the advisory model, I mean, AAA is here to stay. We launched it about a year ago. It's still being consolidated, but we are already -- ready to show that through net inflows or volume and customer experience measured by NPS, that shows that this is an assertive model. It's a model that has the lowest coverage ratio, client versus adviser, and we can give our clients the correct advice.
This is just a consequence of having satisfy customers that bring their volume to us and maintain that volume with us, and that gives us good results. So AAA is moving quite well, performing quite well. Toro is being consolidated. We just acquired the remaining stake. We grew more than 100% year-on-year in terms of net inflows. We have very high NPS.
Toro ranked first or second in terms of NPS consistently, and this is measured by third parties. So Toro is moving and performing quite well. And now with the acquisition of the remaining stake of Toro, we are able to consolidate a lot of the technology and the way of operate. This is a fintech that turned into a digital brokerage firm and we will bring a lot of talent to the people.
And to your right, we have our private banking. I've been talking more and more about our private banking in all dimensions, we have a record funding, record revenue, record results and NPS still very, very high. So private is an essential part of our franchisees, individuals and firms interacting and there is still a lot more to do, but the progress here is very clear.
Slide 8, I am putting more emphasis on the card business. Certainly, the market is very curious about that. They want to know how we are dealing with it, that the active base of clients decrease, the market share decrease. And the answer is yes. In this last conference that I mentioned, I told the market that once we decide to step on the brakes before the rest of the market, at the end of 2021, we knew that, that move would be significant, especially with unsecured products. So we are focusing more on cards rather than personal loans and other products. But in other products, we are focusing on other products as well.
And we knew that in about a year or a year and a half, the share of active customers will decline. We knew that, but it's time now to recover that. And as I said, that we had turned the curve with cards, we are showing now that we are selling a lot more cards than we were selling even in the second quarter and throughout last year in the second -- in the third quarter of 2021, we would sell, I mean, x number of cards. We reduced that to almost 1/3 last quarter and now we are already recovering and achieving a much higher level. It doesn't mean that we reviewed our appetite vis-a-vis 2021. But it means that now we have a much better understanding of our customer base.
All of the investments in CRM that I already mentioned in terms of inter-personalization, this is something quite important because we are working hard in that hyper understanding and knowledge of the client, how they spend their money, I mean their income dynamics and how they perform in the market. So we are working with data architecture and the connection of everything helps us focus better on the client. A lot of these growth in cards come from existing clients and new clients.
And also our strategy in terms of payrolls. So cards is growing. We are very pleased with that. This has already reflected in the fees account, but it will increasingly appear in that fees and margin without letting go of the credit quality, as you can see from the right part of the slide.
Well, we have a loyalty business, which is quite relevant, and that is Esfera. I think we've talked about that. Esfera is a fantastic experience per se. It is connected to the Santander macro system, but this is a business that alone grows almost 60% year-on-year. And it has great penetration with cards. Everything -- every time we have the possibility of selling Esfera and cards, the volume of cards is quite high. I mean volume grew 15% year-on-year. We reduced share and the base of active customers, but we increased by 15%, the client NII. Clients become more connected with us. So they increased their transactions with Santander. In addition to the card itself, they buy and sell using the bank.
Slide 9 here talks about corporate companies. This is another crucial part of our strategy. And I recently talked a lot about that in the media in New York. So we are saying here that we have two large corporate businesses, but they are even more connected in terms of their common parts. And these common parts are technology. Most products are common; and a lot of how I want to position myself, it's common.
We call this one single corporate platform. We've been thinking in a more horizontal way, thinking about corporate and SMEs. Our ambition is to be the bank of all companies. We want to be the bank that corporate and SMEs think about. And they can call us in different formats. In large corporate, we have the natural customization of an investment bank or some more customized transactional services. We are the large international bank of Brazil or the large Brazilian bank with international penetration. We remain #1 in foreign exchange. We are top 3 position in capital markets in terms of net debt over equity.
We are also doing a lot of investments in talent in our people business, and we are very pleased on how things are evolving. We are growing in large corporate. And also SMEs, I've been talking to analysts and investors that we are putting great focus on the increase of our SME business, and I already have some good and solid numbers to show. So SMEs is beginning to respond in our first quarter. We were moving on this side. But consistently, we've been very cautious in the first quarter and last year because we just wanted to see how CDI would evolve, economy was not picking up.
So we made all the necessary adjustments. This quarter, we are beginning to grow. And from now on, in the midterm, we seek to double the business. This is the magnitude of our mission. Now quickly speaking about our strategic business. In the third quarter of '22, I told the market, okay, we continue to pursue our growth history. We will not let go of that. We will seek for a complex portfolio. But at the same time, we choose our levers, and we are growing different levers, not in a linear fashion because that wouldn't be intelligent. But we are growing strongly in all of the levers that we chose.
So this quarter, I'll talk about 3 levers. Our consumer finance. In the third quarter, we are consuming BRL 8.1 billion, and we are growing almost 20% our production towards the third quarter. This certainly brings fees. We know how to do that well. I mean, issues related to spread especially insurance. And because of that, the client NII performs very well. This will appear more significantly in the fourth quarter, and -- but we are not even happy with that number. We have to go for more.
So the consumer finance is an area that was slow in the first quarter, but certainly soon we will increase our appetite to grow. We are very familiar with this business, and I'm sure we can perform even better. In terms of Payroll, we've been consistently telling the market that this is one of the products that we try to work on. It's a very nervous product because the market is very competitive, but we believe we can do that well as well as other players. But we managed to grow above market without letting go of the quality. Our ratings are very good as with consumer finance and cards. So the control side is performing very well, which allows us to grow even more and to grow above the market.
And to conclude, our other major focus is Agro. Agro for the past 5, 6 years is a great focus of Santander, and we are growing. But a year ago, I publicly said that I wanted to reach BRL 70 billion in the portfolio. I mean, Agro clients, they have transaction with non-agro products as well. This is not calculated here. Here, I'm just including agro products and we are almost there. So I shouldn't even give you a spoiler because it seems very likely that we will exceed the target in the fourth quarter. So we will get into 2024 in a very robust situation.
To conclude my presentation, speaking about technology, we could spend hours here talking about technology because that's part of our core strategy in all senior leadership, they are looking at that with first as well. But I'll give you some highlights.
First of all, in a few years, it doubles or triples the volume of transactions. It's even staggering. We talk about in the past 9 months, almost 4 billion transactions. And the volume is very, very high, higher than any comparison that you may have. We know how do we invest. We are very efficient and the cost per transaction drops by half.
So to the right, you have a series of elements that talk about technology, what does technology have to do with customer loyalty, et cetera. We were #1 according to Downdetector. For those of you who are not familiar, this is a public app that checks interferences, bugs, et cetera. We were #1, that means that we are focusing very well in terms of providing the best customer journey. Our app is highly recognized, and this is a very good figure. 84 -- 94% of our transactions occur in the cloud. So we are almost reaching 100%. Just give me a few more quarters, and we will get 100%.
So we have a lot of transaction in the cloud. That means that we are more agile, we are more cost efficient. We have more than 1/4 of additional deployments year-on-year, meaning that we are more agile in terms of improving customer journey and also making corrections along the way and 86% of that occurs automatically and we are maturing. We are deeply maturing our business domains. This means our capacity of no longer being defined according to closed structures or silos, okay?
Operating platforms and technologies they are available to all of our businesses, there are 27 business domains and this is maturing very quickly, and this will really help the customer because the customer is the one that defines how they want us to be organized.
So now I will pause and Gustavo will give you more details on our numbers. Then I will come back at the end. Thank you.
Gustavo Viviani
[Interpreted] Thank you, Mario. Good morning, everyone. So let's start with the performance of our net interest income. We posted total NII growth of 2.1% in the 9 months to date. That means growth in product NII and our portfolio grew within expectations. This quarter, we had a solid growth in asset volumes between the months of the quarter, given the better performance of liabilities that I will talk about later and a better funding result.
In terms of credit growth and greater selectivity since the beginning of 2022, it had an effect on the spreads in the quarter, resulting in a drop of 20 basis points in spread and causing our client NII to fall by 1.3% in the period. As per market operations, we continue to show gradual improvement in our ALM positions given the recent reductions in the Selic rate. This quarter, this improvement was partially offset by lower trading result. We expect the trend of gradual improvements in market operations to continue in the coming quarters and that the client NII will perform better as we grow the portfolio.
Now I will present the evolution of our loan portfolio. We had a better retail performance this quarter and adjusting the consumer portfolio, for the sale of the equity interest in Banco PSA, which happened in August, and as mentioned before, we would have seen a growth of 1.4% in this portfolio, as highlighted here, and individuals in line with what we planned, we had good performance in real estate, payroll loans and rural credit, which has been repeated over the quarters.
I see the evolution of cards increasing 2% as being very positive in the quarter. In auto financing, for individuals, we grew 2.6% quarter-on-quarter. And this was the best performance since December of 2020, excluding the effect of the sale of our equity stake in Banco PSA. This performance is a result of the new strategic partnerships already mentioned.
In SMEs, we were able to resume the growth of our portfolio, thanks to good credit quality indicators, both in short and long term. Growth in the quarter was 3.1%, a level that we haven't seen since the third quarter of last year when we grew due to government programs. Currently, approximately 67% of our total portfolio of loans to individuals, including consumer finance, is secured an increase of 2.5% over the last 12 months.
On the next slide, we provide more details on the breakdown of our balance sheet. We continue to pursue our strategy, as Mario mentioned, of expanding our funding, and we can see growth in funding. I would like to highlight the evolution of the demand deposits growing 10% and time deposits growing 6% in the quarter. The year-on-year evolution is also very satisfactory, mainly due to the participation of retail, which is strategic for us.
Total funding increased 16% in the last 12 months and 4.5% in the quarter. Our loan-to-deposit ratio has shown continuous improvement in the quarter. And we posted the lowest level on record reinforcing the soundness of our balance sheet. Here, we detail the evolution of fees. As Mario said, part of our strategy, which we grew 6.5% in the quarter. We had a very positive performance, as you can see, in practically all fees and commissions lines. The one that performed the best was the insurance business, which benefited from the launch of new products and specific campaigns during the period.
In addition, we continue to perform well in "consórcios" and checking accounts, as you can see from the chart, especially checking accounts due to higher transactionality. So SMEs are growing in loans and fees, that's a good sign. Loans perform better due to the good performance in auto financing and cards, which also performed well in the quarter, growing 2.3%, which is twice the growth when compared to the previous quarter.
Now I will talk about the evolution of the asset quality. The best vintages are gaining relevance and reflect positively on our indicators. Our ALL expense was down 6% in the quarter, and the quarterly cost of credit reached the lowest level since the first quarter of '22. NPL formation has already normalized ending the third quarter at 1.05%. And we again provisioned above the delinquency formation, which brought our coverage level to 230%.
In regards to the renegotiated portfolio, we continue to see a drop in relation to the total portfolio around 30 basis points in the last 12 months, reflecting the effectiveness of all the adjustments made to the risk models in recent months.
Now I will bring some more details on the delinquency indicators. As expected, they continue to show positive trends. NPL over 90 days improved by 30 basis points, both in the individuals and corporate portfolios. The 15- to 90-day NPL showed an improvement of 20 basis points with a positive effect on the individuals portfolio. The corporate and SMEs portfolio showed a slight movie -- movement in the short-term indicator, which is a one-off event that doesn't cause us any concern.
Now moving to Slide 19, we can see the performance of our expenses, which grew by 0.9% in the quarter, very controllable and 7.5% in the 9 months to date. Personnel expenses were impacted by the collective bargaining agreement in recent months. Admin expenses, on the other hand, remain under control. This quarter, we are taking a new look at expenses, separating them into those incurred on products and business expansion and recurring expenses.
The first includes expenses that should support our future growth, such as software amortization, and fees with third parties to boost sales. And we continue to focus on controlling admin expenses, seeking to further improve our efficiency ratio, which improved 70 basis points in the quarter.
And to conclude, I would like to talk about our income statement. As a result of all the dynamics we've talked about so far, we grew our net profit before tax by a significant 32.5%. Our net income, as mentioned before, grew by 18% in the period, and ROE 13.1%, which shows that we are gradually recovering our profitability, a trend that we expect to continue in the coming quarters. Our common equity Tier 1 ratio rose by 50 basis points to 11.2%, mainly due to the entry into force of Resolution 229, which came into effect on July 1 and brought a benefit to our CET1.
With that, I stop now, and I turn the floor back to Mario for his final remarks. So Mario, the floor is yours.
Mario Roberto Leao
[Interpreted] Thank you, Gustavo. So I would just like to conclude with something that consolidates everything we said. What are the main takeaways and I will start with the consolidation of our portfolio management strategy. We had already talked about this in the third -- I mean, the third quarter, we were comfortable because the peak was over. I mean it was clear that the peak was over. We only learned that after the fact.
In the second quarter, we saw that in the third quarter, we consolidated our strategy from 21 continuous months of portfolio management when we grew a lot like the entire market in 2021. And this certainly impacted our results of knowing that we worked in a very quick way to digest that. And now in parallel, we are seeing growth in different areas.
So the first big takeaway is the consolidation of our strategy, which makes us comfortable to show you very clear growth numbers in the portfolios, and we will continue to pursue that in a very consistent manner in the coming quarters.
The second takeaway is that the business where we chose to grow, we are growing, meaning that we are posting a growth history. It doesn't mean that the bottom line grows every quarter. There is no linearly -- linearity, especially in a company of this side -- this size, but we are growing where we wanted to grow and in areas where we knew we had to go slower, we did. And in some cases, we figured that it was time to resume and we're showing good signs.
The third takeaway, great focus on the client, loyalty and how to bring this client to -- more to increase their transactions in the bank. And I will say this constantly. Certainly, we are a bank, so we know and like to grant loans. But even within that loan portfolio, we have to diversify. We have to focus more on mid- and high-income. We would start -- we continue to work with [indiscernible]. We are not just growing for the sake of growing. We're -- this is not a race. And within credit, we want to diversify and also our funding agenda, on balance and off balance.
And to conclude, we also want to pursue obsessively. I know this is a strong word, but we want to obsessively pursue principality. So in addition to that discourse, which is important, we have to look at the details, look at the journey, I mean, look at verbatims from NPS, we have to talk to customers constantly. And also, we have to be humble and listen to our clients.
We know that we still have a lot of things to do. We have to be disciplined. We have to know how to say no when we do have to say no. So with that, I pause, and it's a pleasure to be with you again. And now we pursue -- we go to our Q&A session.
